messages:
sec-bot: New CVE ingested: CVE-2026-0456 affecting grpcio (python). CVSS: 9.1, EPSS: 0.72. Link: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-0456

maya: Heads-up — looks high severity. NVD notes remote code execution via crafted metadata frames. We use grpcio in multiple places (ingest, controller). Need initial scope and exploitability checks.

jonathan: On it. Quick questions: any public PoC yet?

maya: No confirmed PoC from vendor advisory at first glance. Some tweets claiming partial PoC but unverified. Vendor says patch available in grpcio 1.56.3+ and 1.57.0.

alejandra: I can run a repo grep and image scan. Running locally: `rg \"grpcio\" -S | head` to find pinned deps. Will post results.

alejandra: Found grpcio in: `services/ingest/requirements.txt` pinned to 1.55.2, `runtime/pyproject.toml` uses >=1.54,<1.57, and `third_party/legacy/` wheels vendored.

samir: Also check k8s node images — some containers build from pip wheels at build-time. If wheel vendored we need rebuild CI images asap.

jonathan: Exploitability checklist I'm running: 1) reachable attack surface (ingest externally facing?) 2) auth/RBAC barriers 3) whether we pass untrusted metadata frames from clients 4) can we trigger with our client versions.

maya: Quick risk notes: public-facing ingest (api-redwood) terminates TLS and proxies to internal grpc services. If grpc connection between proxy and service accepts metadata frames from upstream, RCE could be possible. Also check any internal admin endpoints that accept client-provided metadata.

alejandra: Image scan (Trivy) results: found grpcio 1.55.2 in 3 images (ingest, eval-runner, model-manager). No PoC found in logs.

jonathan: I'm checking access logs for odd metadata headers. Ran `kubectl logs` on ingest proxy — nothing suspicious. But assume exploitation possible until patched.

maya: Prioritization recommendation: P0/P1? Given CVSS 9.1 and EPSS 0.72, and presence in external-facing ingest, I recommend P1 (patch within 24h) with mitigations for P0 if evidence of active exploit.

samir: Can we mitigate without full patch? Options: 1) add an Envoy filter to drop grpc metadata frames at edge 2) fail-open -> deny untrusted metadata 3) temporary WAF rule to block suspicious payloads. Envoy filter seems quickest.

alejandra: I can push an Envoy config change to strip `grpc-*` metadata and restart proxies — low risk. Also start builds for patched images (upgrade to 1.56.3).

jonathan: I'll open a dedicated incident ticket and run an image rebuild job: `./ci/rebuild-images --service ingest,eval-runner,model-manager --pip grpcio==1.56.3`. ETA: 6h for build + deploy to canary.

maya: Good. Also need to consider key material: if any KMS clients use grpcio code paths and could have had in-memory compromise, do we rotate keys? I think not yet unless evidence of compromise, but enable stricter audit logging for KMS calls for 72h.

samir: KMS audit logging: enabling at control plane now. I'll also add an alert for unusual key-decrypt counts.

alejandra: Pushed Envoy strip rule to canary ingress. Canary metrics looking normal after 10m. No errors in downstream services.

jonathan: Canary image with grpcio 1.56.3 deployed to 10% traffic. Running smoke tests (end-to-end, long-poll).

maya: Action items summary (assigned):
- aleajandra: rebuild and push patched images (due 6h)
- jonathan: incident ticket + deploy canary + smoke tests (in progress)
- samir: enable KMS audit + alerts (done)
- maya: monitor CVE feeds for PoC + coordinate communications with ops and legal (owner)

maya: Marking severity P1 for now. If we detect active exploitation escalate to P0 and rotate affected keys.

jonathan: I'll post status updates to #incidents and ping infra on pager if any anomalies.

sec-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-311. Tags: cve, grpcio, patching. Assigned: eng-security, eng-runtime, eng-sre.

alejandra: Noted. I found one legacy container image in `third_party/legacy/old-worker` that vendors grpcio wheel; creating patch PR to remove vendor wheel and pin to 1.56.3.

maya: Thanks — please include migration note in the PR so release engineer can rebuild images without downtime.

jonathan: Update 2h: no anomalous traffic, canary looks healthy. Rolling to 50% next.

maya: Good work. We'll reconvene if PoC appears. For now keep monitoring logs, rotate to patched images, and keep KMS audit on for 72h.
